welcome: I am the Guide Bot for this Amazon Connect lab. I only repeat what a page here already says, and I name the source. I do not invent a port, a price, or a date.
fallback: I do not have a cited page in this lab for that. I will not guess. Open Search, or ask about UDP 3478, Lambda, Voice ID, the 4 August 2026 names, Global Resiliency, E911, or the Ecosystem track.

steps.say: Diagrams are the large pictures. Each caption names the admin-guide page it came from.
Flows are the animated hop diagrams. The moving dot is the contact or the signal.
Charts use the quota table and the 14 October 2026 price appendix. They are teaching shapes when the caption says so.
Cheat Codes are one-page sheets. Each has HTML, PDF, and PNG.
Ecosystem is the work beside the queue: forecasting, recording, E911, the CRM, and agent assist.

quiz.q: Which UDP port does the softphone use toward TurnNlb?
quiz.why: Sign-in can use TCP 443 while media is outbound UDP 3478 to the Regional TurnNlb domain.

quiz.q: How long does a synchronous Lambda block wait?
quiz.why: The synchronous invoke cap in this lab is 8 seconds. The block's own timeout can be shorter. Async work uses a different pattern.

quiz.q: When did Voice ID support end?
quiz.why: New customers stopped on 20 May 2025. Support ended on 20 May 2026. Remove Set Voice ID and Check Voice ID from a 2026 flow.

quiz.q: What did the admin guide call Contact Lens after 4 August 2026?
quiz.why: On 4 August 2026 the documented rename is Contact Lens to conversational analytics, Amazon Q in Connect to agent assist, and Voice+ to Live Sync.

entries.title: UDP 3478
entries.answer: The CCP can sign in on TCP 443 while media fails. Softphone media is outbound UDP 3478 to TurnNlb-*.elb.<region>.amazonaws.com. A stateless firewall also needs the browser's ephemeral UDP return range, and this lab does not invent that range.

entries.title: TCP 443
entries.answer: TCP 443 is the signaling and admin path. Opening only 443 does not open media. Media is still UDP 3478.

entries.title: Lambda contract
entries.answer: A synchronous Invoke AWS Lambda function block waits at most 8 seconds. The response the block validates is a string map unless you choose JSON. AccessDenied in the flow log means the function never ran.

entries.title: Voice ID
entries.answer: Voice ID stopped taking new customers on 20 May 2025 and support ended on 20 May 2026. A 2026 flow should not contain Set Voice ID or Check Voice ID.

entries.title: 4 August 2026 names
entries.answer: The timeline this lab cites for 4 August 2026 says the admin guide renamed Contact Lens to conversational analytics, Amazon Q in Connect to agent assist, forecasting capacity planning and scheduling to forecasting and agent scheduling, and Voice+ to Live Sync.

entries.title: Global Resiliency
entries.answer: Global Resiliency is the supported multi-Region design. Published pairs are Northern Virginia with Oregon, Frankfurt with London, and Tokyo with Osaka. Telephony shifts in 10 percent steps. Osaka delivery can take up to 20 seconds.

entries.title: US emergency calling
entries.answer: For US CCP agents, validate the address, store it on the agent profile, and read it back with 933. This lab never places a live 911 call. Direct 911 from the CCP is documented for US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and GovCloud US-West.

entries.title: Chat concurrency
entries.answer: The default concurrent chat ceiling in the quota table is 500, shared with SMS, WhatsApp, and Apple Messages for Business. An idle chat still counts.

entries.title: Badges are not exams
entries.answer: There is no AWS Certified Amazon Connect specialty exam in the catalog this lab cites. Connect Skill Builder badges pass at 80 percent. That badge is not the Solutions Architect exam.

entries.title: Oregon DID example
entries.answer: The worked example this lab dates 14 October 2026 is a US DID in Oregon at 0.030 USD per day and 0.0022 USD per inbound minute. Country rates that are not in that example are not invented here.
entries.source: Connect Customer pricing appendix, read 14 October 2026

entries.title: Ecosystem
entries.answer: Connect owns the live contact. Forecasting and scheduling own the shift. Recording owns the proof. The CRM owns the person. E911 owns the agent's location on a 911 call. Agent assist owns a recommendation, not the decision. Sister systems need ContactId or they cannot be audited.

entries.title: Flow types
entries.answer: Inbound, customer queue, hold, whisper, transfer, and disconnect flows are different canvases. A hold flow is not where you transfer to a queue. End flow / Resume does not hang up. Disconnect does.

entries.title: Queues and profiles
entries.answer: A queue holds the contact. A routing profile decides who is eligible. The default is 100 queues per instance. Lower priority number is offered first. Delay holds a second team in reserve.

entries.title: Lucky
entries.answer: Lucky is a lifelong student and an AI enthusiast, from systems, networking, voice, and the contact center, growing into AI omni-channel agents. This campus is that study. It is wider than a UC engineer.

entries.title: Cheat codes
entries.answer: Cheat Codes are one-page HTML, PDF, and PNG sheets for ports, call flows, cutover, the firewall matrix, careers, E911, WFM, and the 2026 timeline.
